newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CUBS SIGN CLOSER ROJAS TO THREE-YEAR DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CUBS SIGN CLOSER ROJAS TO THREE-YEAR DEAL.

text.p: Free agent relief ace Mel Rojas celebrated his 30th birthday Tuesday by signing a three-year deal with the Chicago Cubs.
Financial terms were not disclosed, but WMVP Radio in Chicago reported the deal to be worth $13.5 million.
Rojas, granted free agency when the new labour deal was ratified, has spent all seven of his major-league seasons with the Montreal Expos. The Dominican's uncle, Felipe Alou, is the Montreal manager.
Rojas took over as the Expos' closer when John Wetteland went to the New York Yankees two seasons ago.
In 74 games last season, Rojas was 7-4 with a 3.22 ERA and 36 saves in 40 opportunities. Rojas's save percentage of .900 was tops in the National League.
Rojas has appeared in 385 games, all in relief. His career record is 29-23 with a 3.04 ERA, with saves in 109 of 138 chances.
The Cubs used a bullpen by committee last season after free agent Randy Myers signed with Baltimore. Turk Wendell led the team in saves with 18.

Rojas is yet another star player to leave the cost-cutting Expos via a trade for free agency, joining Wetteland, Ken Hill, Dennis Martinez, Larry Walker, Marquis Grissom and Jeff Fassero in recent seasons.
